sources.title: Higher derivative couplings of hypermultiplets

evidence.text: The higher-derivative hypermultiplet ansatz contains 33 coefficients. The authors organize independent supersymmetry variations into a reported system of 58 equations for 35 parameters, first treating structures independent of H and the dilaton gradient, then examining the remaining structures.

sources.title: Higher derivative couplings with multi-tensor multiplets in 6D supergravity, action and anomalies

evidence.text: Use the ADM time-space split and Henneaux–Teitelboim Hamiltonian formulation. Only spatial two-form components enter the action; the Poincaré lemma integrates their Euler–Lagrange equations to the duality equations, introducing temporal components as integration data.

sources.title: Higher derivative couplings of hypermultiplets

evidence.text: An on-shell Noether procedure requires δ0L1 to vanish modulo the lowest-order field equations Eφ. Remaining terms f(ε,φ)Eφ determine first-order transformation corrections δ1φ=−f(ε,φ), rather than requiring an off-shell hypermultiplet formulation.

sources.title: Higher derivative couplings of hypermultiplets

evidence.text: The known Yang–Mills-to-Lorentz map replaces (AμI,λI) with the torsionful connection and gravitino curvature (Ω−μrs,ψrs) to generate the BdR curvature-squared sector. Linear-H variations subsequently require additional hyperino bilinears LH; dilaton-gradient variations require no new terms after imposing the coefficient solution.

sources.title: Higher derivative couplings with multi-tensor multiplets in 6D supergravity, action and anomalies

evidence.text: Use superconformal tensor calculus and the Bergshoeff–de Roo map: identify a torsionful spin connection, gravitino curvature and auxiliary curvature with an off-shell Yang–Mills multiplet. Pull back its invariant through an embedding valid modulo two-derivative equations. The perturbative Noether/BV discussion permits field redefinitions, subject to stated complications.
